title: Nonintrusive observation proxy with cost‑bounded stochastic duplication
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a noninvasive observation proxy that duplicates production requests to candidate model endpoints for telemetry and quality evaluation while enforcing strict cost and tenant isolation controls. The proxy must ensure no added latency to primary responses, provide per-tenant credit accounting for mirrored traffic, and support adaptive stochastic sampling driven by budget and signal quality.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy duplicates requests asynchronously: primary path latency increase < 0.5ms p95 under steady state
Per-tenant mirror spend tracked and exposed to billing pipeline (metered tags and counters)
Sampling algorithm implements credit‑bound token bucket and decays sample rate when spend threshold reached
Canary/control plane sees mirrored outputs in real time with <5s delivery for live evaluators
Mirrored requests run in isolated ephemeral sandboxes (no writes to downstream systems)
Rollout controller can call numeric regressions from mirrored telemetry to trigger automatic pause/rollback
Integration tests validate that mirrored traffic never mutates production state and that replay logs are complete for offline evaluation
plan: Design: finalize proxy contract and handshake with routing/Gateway team (2 days)
Implement observation proxy sidecar with async duplication channel and local buffer (10 days)
Add per-tenant credit accounting store and expose read/write hooks for billing (4 days)
Integrate sampling policy engine: credit token bucket + workload jitter + emergency caps (6 days)
Sandbox runner: run mirrored requests against candidate in restricted env with network egress blocked, disk ephemeral (6 days)
Telemetry: add mirror keystats, cost tags, mirrored-latency histogram and delivery lag metric (3 days)
End-to-end tests: mutation-safety, budget-enforcement, auto-rollback signal path (5 days)
Docs & runbook: operator playbook for quarantining noisy tenants and inspecting mirror accounting (2 days)
notes: Trade-off: Synchronous duplication would simplify observability but risks latency and user impact — chosen async with local buffer and best-effort delivery.
We will prioritize low-overhead telemetry (sampled histograms) to avoid duplicating entire payloads in metrics storage.
Decision: mirrored requests should be marked immutable and routed through a network ACL that forbids writes to any production databases or external APIs.
We will provide an opt-in tenant flag to enable richer mirroring payloads (full context) for trusted customers during early trials.
Prototype shows that a 1% baseline sampling with credit refill rate covers most QA needs for small tenants while keeping cost under 0.2% of total spend.
Coordination required with Billing team to map mirror events to chargeable units and avoid double-billing hosted tokens.
risks: Burst amplification: correlated spikes in mirrored delivery may overwhelm sandbox runners — mitigated by backpressure and per-tenant circuit breakers
Silent drift: candidate model responses batched/delivered out-of-order could confuse live evaluators — include sequence IDs and delivery lag metrics
Cost underrun/overrun: inaccurate credit accounting leads to overspend — add conservative caps and daily reconciliation job
Privacy/regulatory: mirrored payloads may contain sensitive attributes — ensure PII redaction pipeline and opt-in policies for private deployments
Operational complexity: additional moving parts (sidecars, sandboxes, accounting store) increase debugging surface — include detailed tracing and single-click diagnostic dump
